title: North Carolina History (8th Grade)
description: North Carolina History (8th Grade) practice - 100 questions

questions.question: Long before Europeans arrived, the largest and most powerful Indigenous nation in the North Carolina mountains was the:
questions.correctAnswer: Cherokee, whose towns stretched across the southern Appalachian Mountains
distractors: Sioux, whose towns stretched across the southern Appalachian Mountains
Iroquois, whose towns stretched across the southern Appalachian Mountains
Apache, whose towns stretched across the southern Appalachian Mountains
questions.explanation: The Cherokee were the dominant nation in North Carolina's mountain region, with dozens of towns along the rivers of the southern Appalachians. Their descendants, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, still live on the Qualla Boundary today.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cherokee in the Carolina mountains - the name still on the map today.

img.tip: The Cherokee were the major Indigenous nation of North Carolina's mountain region.
img.title: CHEROKEE HOMELAND

questions.question: In 1587, John White's colony on Roanoke Island became famous in history because:
questions.correctAnswer: The colonists vanished, leaving only the word CROATOAN carved on a post - it became the Lost Colony
distractors: It was the first English colony to grow tobacco for export to Europe
Its settlers signed a peace treaty that ended all wars with the Secotan
It defeated a Spanish fleet sent to destroy it
questions.explanation: When John White returned from England in 1590 after a three-year delay, the roughly 115 Roanoke colonists were gone. The only clue was CROATOAN carved on a palisade post, and the colony's fate remains one of America's oldest mysteries.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One carved word, zero colonists - CROATOAN is the whole clue.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of an empty 1580s English island settlement on the North Carolina coast, wooden palisade and small empty houses, a single post with carved marks in the foreground, quiet shoreline and pine forest. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Roanoke's settlers disappeared; CROATOAN was the only clue left behind.
img.title: THE LOST COLONY

questions.question: Virginia Dare, born on Roanoke Island in August 1587, is remembered as:
questions.correctAnswer: The first English child born in the Americas
distractors: The first English child to attend school in the Americas
The author of the first book published in the colonies
The woman who later founded the town of Bath
questions.explanation: Virginia Dare was the granddaughter of Governor John White and the first child of English parents born in the New World. She disappeared with the rest of the Lost Colony, and her story became a lasting symbol of Roanoke Island.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Virginia Dare - first English baby born across the sea.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a 1580s English colonial family on a Carolina barrier island holding a newborn infant wrapped in linen, wooden stockade and the sea behind them, soft morning light. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Virginia Dare was the first English child born in the Americas.
img.title: VIRGINIA DARE

questions.question: The town of Bath, incorporated in 1705, holds which distinction in North Carolina history?
questions.correctAnswer: It is North Carolina's oldest town
distractors: It was the colony's first capital city
It was where the first NC constitution was written
It was the site of the first gold discovery in America
questions.explanation: Bath, on the Pamlico River, was incorporated in 1705 and is the oldest town in North Carolina. The pirate Blackbeard later lived there for a time, and it served as an early port and meeting place for the colonial assembly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bath came first - 1705, the oldest town in the state.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a small early 1700s Carolina port town on a calm river, a few wooden and brick houses, a church steeple, sailing shallops at a wharf, marsh grass along the shore. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Bath (1705) is North Carolina's oldest incorporated town.
img.title: OLDEST TOWN: BATH

questions.question: New Bern, founded in 1710 by Swiss and German settlers, got its name from:
questions.correctAnswer: Bern, the Swiss home city of its founder, Baron von Graffenried
distractors: A Tuscarora word meaning place of the pine trees
The English city of Berne-upon-Tweed
Governor Edward Hyde's family estate in England
questions.explanation: Christoph von Graffenried led Swiss and German Palatine settlers to the meeting of the Trent and Neuse rivers in 1710 and named their town New Bern after Bern, Switzerland. New Bern later became the colonial capital.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: New Bern is named like a Swiss souvenir - Bern, with 'New' in front.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of settlers in early 1700s European dress clearing land and raising timber houses where two wide rivers meet in coastal North Carolina, boats unloading supplies. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: New Bern was named for Bern, Switzerland, its founder's home.
img.title: NAMING NEW BERN

questions.question: The Tuscarora War (1711-1715) in North Carolina was mainly caused by:
questions.correctAnswer: Colonists seizing Tuscarora land and traders kidnapping and enslaving Native people
distractors: A Tuscarora alliance with Spain to invade the colony
A dispute over which tribe could trade with Virginia
Colonial taxes placed on Tuscarora corn
questions.explanation: Settlers around Bath and New Bern took Tuscarora land, and dishonest traders cheated and enslaved Native people. In September 1711 the Tuscarora and their allies struck back, beginning a devastating war that ended with many Tuscarora migrating north to join the Iroquois Confederacy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stolen land and stolen people lit the Tuscarora War.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of Tuscarora families leaving their Carolina homeland on a long northward journey at dawn, carrying bundles along a forest river path, distant smoke over an abandoned village. Somber tone. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Land seizures and enslavement of Native people drove the Tuscarora to war.
img.title: THE TUSCARORA WAR

questions.question: The pirate Blackbeard, who accepted a royal pardon and lived in Bath, was killed in 1718 at:
questions.correctAnswer: Ocracoke Inlet, in a battle with a Virginia naval force
distractors: Cape Fear, when his ship ran aground in a storm
Roanoke Island, by the crew of his own ship
Charleston harbor, after a siege of the city
questions.explanation: Blackbeard (Edward Teach) settled briefly in Bath after accepting a pardon, but Virginia's governor sent Lieutenant Robert Maynard against him anyway. Maynard's force killed Blackbeard at Ocracoke Inlet in November 1718, ending his career on the Carolina coast.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Blackbeard's last fight was at Ocracoke, 1718.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of two small 1718 naval sloops locked together in a misty Carolina inlet at dawn, sailors in period dress on deck, low sandy island and lighthouse-less shoreline behind. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Blackbeard was killed at Ocracoke Inlet in 1718.
img.title: BLACKBEARD AT OCRACOKE

questions.question: Backcountry farmers called the Regulators rose up in the 1760s mainly because they believed:
questions.correctAnswer: Local officials were corrupt and charged illegal fees while courts ignored their complaints
distractors: The governor had banned farming west of the mountains
Britain had stationed soldiers in their homes
The assembly had outlawed the Presbyterian church
questions.explanation: Piedmont and backcountry farmers formed the Regulator movement to protest corrupt sheriffs, unjust fees, and courts that served wealthy eastern interests. Their petitions and protests were repeatedly ignored, pushing the movement toward open confrontation with Governor Tryon.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Regulators wanted honest fees and fair courts - regulation, not independence.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of backcountry North Carolina farmers in 1760s work clothes gathered outside a small wooden courthouse, holding a petition, log cabins and split-rail fences behind them. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The Regulators protested corrupt officials, illegal fees, and unfair courts.
img.title: THE REGULATORS

questions.question: The Battle of Alamance on May 16, 1771, ended when:
questions.correctAnswer: Governor William Tryon's militia defeated the Regulators, crushing the movement
distractors: The Regulators defeated the governor and won control of the colony
Both sides agreed to a treaty written at Hillsborough
British regulars arrived and arrested Governor Tryon
questions.explanation: At Alamance Creek, Governor Tryon's well-supplied militia of about 1,000 men defeated roughly 2,000 poorly armed Regulators. Several Regulator leaders were later hanged, and the movement collapsed - five years before the Revolution began.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Alamance, 1771 - Tryon won, and the Regulator movement ended.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of an 18th-century militia encampment beside a wide creek in the North Carolina piedmont at dusk, rows of tents and a cannon, somber smoke on the horizon. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Governor Tryon's militia won at Alamance in 1771 and crushed the Regulators.
img.title: BATTLE OF ALAMANCE

questions.question: On October 25, 1774, Penelope Barker led 51 women of Edenton in an action remembered as the Edenton Tea Party. What did they do?
questions.correctAnswer: They signed a public resolution promising to boycott British tea and cloth
distractors: They dumped a cargo of British tea into the harbor
They marched on the governor's palace in New Bern
They hid weapons for the colonial militia
questions.explanation: The Edenton women signed their names to a boycott of British goods - one of the first organized political actions by women in American history. British newspapers mocked them in cartoons, which only spread their fame further.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fifty-one signatures, no dumped tea - Edenton protested with a pen.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of colonial-era women in 1770s dress gathered around a table in a coastal North Carolina home, signing a large paper resolution by candlelight, teacups untouched beside them. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The Edenton women signed a boycott resolution - an early women's political protest.
img.title: THE EDENTON TEA PARTY

questions.question: The Mecklenburg Resolves, adopted in Charlotte in May 1775, declared that:
questions.correctAnswer: British authority in the colony was suspended and local committees would govern
distractors: North Carolina was an independent nation
All British soldiers must leave Boston within a month
The colony would remain loyal if taxes were lowered
questions.explanation: Meeting in Charlotte after news of Lexington and Concord, Mecklenburg County leaders declared British laws and authority null and void and set up local rule. North Carolinians also honor a claimed May 20, 1775 declaration - the date appears on the state flag alongside April 12, 1776.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mecklenburg said British rule was suspended - local committees took over.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of colonial county leaders in 1775 dress meeting inside a log courthouse in a small Carolina town, reading a proclamation aloud to a crowd outside the door. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The Mecklenburg Resolves suspended British authority and set up local government.
img.title: MECKLENBURG RESOLVES

questions.question: The Halifax Resolves of April 12, 1776, were historic because North Carolina became the first colony to:
questions.correctAnswer: Officially authorize its delegates to vote for independence from Britain
distractors: Ratify the Declaration of Independence
Abolish slavery within its borders
Elect a governor by popular vote
questions.explanation: Meeting at Halifax, the Fourth Provincial Congress voted unanimously to empower North Carolina's delegates in Philadelphia to join in declaring independence. It was the first official action by any colony toward independence - which is why April 12, 1776 appears on the North Carolina state flag.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Halifax, April 12, 1776 - first colony to say yes to independence.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of a colonial provincial congress in 1776 seated in a modest wooden hall in a small river town, delegates raising hands in a unanimous vote, spring light through tall windows. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The Halifax Resolves first authorized delegates to vote for independence (April 12, 1776).
img.title: THE HALIFAX RESOLVES

questions.question: At the Battle of Moore's Creek Bridge (February 27, 1776), North Carolina Patriots won by:
questions.correctAnswer: Removing the bridge planks and greasing the girders, then firing on the Loyalist Highland Scots as they tried to cross
distractors: Flooding the creek with a broken mill dam
Charging across the bridge ahead of the Loyalists
Setting fire to the surrounding pine forest
questions.explanation: Patriot forces pulled up the planks of the bridge over Moore's Creek and greased the remaining girders. When the Loyalist Highlanders charged across in the dark with broadswords, they were met by cannon and musket fire. The quick victory ended royal authority in North Carolina and pushed the colony toward the Halifax Resolves.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No planks, greased beams, one volley - Moore's Creek Bridge.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of a narrow wooden bridge with its planks removed over a dark swampy creek at night in 1776, patriot militia waiting silently behind earthworks on the far bank, cypress trees and Spanish moss. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Patriots stripped and greased the bridge at Moore's Creek and ambushed the Loyalists.
img.title: MOORE'S CREEK BRIDGE

questions.question: Richard Caswell, commander of the Patriot force at Moore's Creek Bridge, next became:
questions.correctAnswer: The first governor of the independent state of North Carolina
distractors: The first president of the University of North Carolina
Commander of the Continental Army in the South
The state's first United States senator
questions.explanation: Richard Caswell led the Patriots at Moore's Creek and presided over the congress that wrote North Carolina's first constitution in 1776. Under that constitution he became the state's first governor, serving from 1776 to 1780.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Caswell won the bridge battle, then became governor number one.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of a dignified 1770s North Carolina statesman in a dark coat standing before a colonial assembly hall, holding a rolled constitution document, early state flags without readable symbols behind him. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Richard Caswell, the Moore's Creek commander, was North Carolina's first governor.
img.title: GOVERNOR CASWELL

questions.question: North Carolina's first constitution, written at Halifax in late 1776, opened with a separate document called the:
questions.correctAnswer: North Carolina Declaration of Rights, listing freedoms the government could not violate
distractors: Carolina Charter of Liberties
Halifax Bill of Complaints
Fundamental Constitutions of Carolina
questions.explanation: Before framing the government itself, the Halifax convention adopted a Declaration of Rights - 25 sections protecting rights such as trial by jury, freedom of the press, and freedom of worship. That tradition continues today: the Declaration of Rights is Article I of the modern NC Constitution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rights first, government second - the Declaration of Rights opens the NC Constitution.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of delegates in 1776 dress drafting a large handwritten document at a long table in a plain hall, quills and candles, a simple list layout on the page with no readable words. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The 1776 NC Constitution opened with a Declaration of Rights guarding the people's freedoms.
img.title: DECLARATION OF RIGHTS

questions.question: The twin dates on the North Carolina state flag - May 20, 1775 and April 12, 1776 - honor:
questions.correctAnswer: The Mecklenburg action in Charlotte and the Halifax Resolves, two early steps toward independence
distractors: The founding of Charlotte and the founding of Raleigh
The battles of King's Mountain and Guilford Courthouse
Statehood day and the opening of the first university
questions.explanation: The flag carries the two dates North Carolina claims as firsts in the independence story: the May 1775 Mecklenburg action against British authority and April 12, 1776, when the Halifax Resolves made NC the first colony to authorize a vote for independence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two dates on the flag - Charlotte and Halifax, 1775 and 1776.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of a state flag with a red white and blue design flying over a green Carolina landscape at sunrise, shown at a distance so no lettering is readable, scroll shapes suggested on the flag. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The flag's two dates honor the Mecklenburg action and the Halifax Resolves.
img.title: TWO DATES ON THE FLAG

questions.question: At the Battle of King's Mountain (October 7, 1780), Patriot militia from the Carolina backcountry destroyed a Loyalist force. The battle mattered because it:
questions.correctAnswer: Forced the British to abandon their plan to rally Loyalists and conquer the backcountry
distractors: Captured the British army of General Cornwallis
Won French recognition of American independence
Opened the port of Wilmington to American shipping
questions.explanation: Overmountain Men and backcountry militia surrounded Major Patrick Ferguson's Loyalists on King's Mountain and destroyed the force in about an hour. The defeat wrecked Cornwallis's strategy of winning the South through Loyalist support and revived Patriot morale.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: King's Mountain broke the British plan to win the South with Loyalists.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of backcountry militia riflemen in hunting shirts climbing a wooded rocky ridge in autumn 1780, long rifles in hand, morning mist in the valley below. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: King's Mountain destroyed the Loyalist force and wrecked the British southern strategy.
img.title: KING'S MOUNTAIN

questions.question: The Battle of Guilford Courthouse (March 15, 1781) is best described as a:
questions.correctAnswer: British victory so costly that Cornwallis lost about a quarter of his army and soon abandoned North Carolina
distractors: Decisive American victory that captured the British army
Naval battle fought in the Cape Fear River
Battle in which no shots were fired
questions.explanation: General Nathanael Greene's army, built heavily on North Carolina militia, lost the field at Guilford Courthouse but shattered Cornwallis's army in the process. Cornwallis retreated to Wilmington and then marched to Virginia - and Yorktown - never returning to conquer North Carolina.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Greene lost the field but won the campaign - Guilford bled Cornwallis dry.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of an 18th-century battlefield in rolling Carolina farmland and woods in early spring, militia lines among fence rails, distant smoke, a small courthouse building on a rise. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Guilford Courthouse cost Cornwallis a quarter of his army; he soon left North Carolina.
img.title: GUILFORD COURTHOUSE

questions.question: Tryon Palace in New Bern, completed in 1770, was built as:
questions.correctAnswer: The grand home and government seat of the royal governor, William Tryon
distractors: A royal navy fort guarding the Neuse River
The first capitol of the independent state
A prison for captured Regulator leaders
questions.explanation: Governor William Tryon built the elegant palace as both his residence and the colony's seat of government. Backcountry taxpayers who had to pay for it resented it bitterly - one more grievance behind the Regulator movement. The restored palace now stands in New Bern as a historic site.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tryon's palace looked royal - and taxpayers noticed.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of an elegant Georgian brick governor's palace in 1770 with formal gardens, a center main house and two side wings, on a riverfront in coastal North Carolina, horse-drawn carriage in front. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Tryon Palace was the royal governor's home and seat of government in New Bern.
img.title: TRYON PALACE

questions.question: In 1788, North Carolina's Hillsborough Convention refused to ratify the new United States Constitution. The main reason was that:
questions.correctAnswer: The Constitution lacked a bill of rights protecting individual freedoms
distractors: North Carolina wanted to remain a British colony
The Constitution gave North Carolina too many representatives
Delegates believed the capital should be in North Carolina
questions.explanation: Anti-Federalist delegates at Hillsborough voted neither to ratify nor reject but demanded amendments first - above all a bill of rights. Only after Congress approved the Bill of Rights did North Carolina ratify, at Fayetteville in November 1789, becoming the twelfth state.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No bill of rights, no ratification - NC waited until 1789.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of delegates debating in a plain 1788 meeting hall in a small Carolina town, some standing and gesturing, papers on long tables, late summer light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: NC refused to ratify in 1788 because the Constitution had no bill of rights.
img.title: HILLSBOROUGH SAYS WAIT

questions.question: North Carolina finally ratified the United States Constitution at Fayetteville in November 1789, making it the:
questions.correctAnswer: Twelfth state to join the Union
distractors: Ninth state to join the Union
Thirteenth and last of the original states
First state to join the Union
questions.explanation: After Congress sent the Bill of Rights to the states, a second convention at Fayetteville ratified the Constitution in November 1789. North Carolina was the twelfth state; only Rhode Island held out longer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Twelfth in - NC joined once the Bill of Rights was on its way.

img.scene: Solemn mature educational illustration of delegates in late 1780s dress celebrating outside a brick market house in a Carolina town, shaking hands, autumn trees and a crowd of townspeople. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: NC ratified at Fayetteville in 1789 as the twelfth state.
img.title: TWELFTH STATE

questions.question: The area of North Carolina west of the mountains was ceded to the United States in 1789 and soon became the state of:
questions.correctAnswer: Tennessee
distractors: Kentucky
West Virginia
Ohio
questions.explanation: North Carolina once stretched to the Mississippi River. In 1789 it ceded its western lands to the federal government; those lands formed the Southwest Territory and entered the Union as Tennessee in 1796.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tennessee used to be western North Carolina.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a parchment-style map scene with two large shaded land regions divided by a bold mountain range, a river flowing west, quill and compass on the table beside it, without any labels or markings. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: NC ceded its western lands in 1789; they became Tennessee.
img.title: THE WESTERN CESSION

questions.question: In 1838, most Cherokee in North Carolina were forced west on the Trail of Tears. The Cherokee who remained in the state became known as the:
questions.correctAnswer: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, centered on the Qualla Boundary
distractors: Lumbee Tribe of the Coastal Plain
Catawba Nation of the Piedmont
Western Band of the Smoky Mountains
questions.explanation: Federal troops rounded up the Cherokee in 1838 for forced removal to Oklahoma; thousands died on the journey. Some Cherokee hid in the mountains or held land through William Holland Thomas, and their descendants form the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, whose Qualla Boundary land lies near today's town of Cherokee.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Eastern Band stayed - their home is the Qualla Boundary.

img.scene: Somber mature educational illustration of Cherokee families walking a mountain forest trail in 1838 carrying bundles, soldiers on horseback at a distance, cold mist among bare trees. Somber tone. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Cherokee who remained in NC became the Eastern Band on the Qualla Boundary.
img.title: THE EASTERN BAND

questions.question: The Cherokee man Tsali became a folk hero in North Carolina because, according to tradition, he:
questions.correctAnswer: Surrendered and gave his life so that a remnant of Cherokee families could remain hidden in the mountains
distractors: Led the Cherokee army to victory at Horseshoe Bend
Wrote the first Cherokee-language newspaper in the state
Discovered gold on Cherokee land near Charlotte
questions.explanation: During the 1838 removal, Tsali and his sons escaped after killing soldiers who had abused his family. By tradition, Tsali surrendered once the army agreed the remaining hidden Cherokee could stay; he and two sons were executed. His sacrifice is remembered as the reason an Eastern Band survived in North Carolina.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tsali's sacrifice is remembered as the price of the Eastern Band's survival.

img.scene: Somber mature educational illustration of an elderly Cherokee man standing calmly at the edge of a misty mountain forest clearing at dawn, families watching from the trees behind him, deep stillness. Somber tone. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Tradition says Tsali gave his life so hidden Cherokee families could remain.
img.title: TSALI'S SACRIFICE

questions.question: Slavery in early North Carolina differed from South Carolina and Virginia mainly in that:
questions.correctAnswer: North Carolina had fewer huge plantations; many enslaved people worked on small farms, in towns, and in trades
distractors: Slavery was illegal in North Carolina until 1800
Enslaved people in North Carolina could vote in county elections
North Carolina imported enslaved people directly from Africa in large numbers
questions.explanation: North Carolina's coast lacked deep-water ports for the largest plantation trade, and its economy leaned on smaller farms producing tobacco, corn, and naval stores. By 1860 about one in three North Carolinians was enslaved - slavery shaped every part of life even without giant plantation districts on the South Carolina scale.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Smaller farms, same injustice - about one in three North Carolinians was enslaved by 1860.

img.scene: Somber mature educational illustration of enslaved workers harvesting tobacco on a modest North Carolina farm in the early 1800s, a small farmhouse and curing barn, fields stretching toward pine woods. Somber tone, no individuals in distress shown graphically. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: NC slavery centered on smaller farms and trades rather than giant plantations.
img.title: SLAVERY IN NORTH CAROLINA

questions.question: In 1799, twelve-year-old Conrad Reed found a shiny 17-pound rock in a creek on his father's farm in Cabarrus County. That rock was:
questions.correctAnswer: Gold - the first documented gold discovery in the United States, starting America's first gold rush in North Carolina
distractors: A meteorite that became the first specimen in the state museum
Copper that opened the colony's first mine
A diamond that made the Reed family the richest in the state
questions.explanation: The Reed family used the heavy yellow rock as a doorstop for years before a jeweler recognized it as gold. The Reed Gold Mine discovery launched the nation's first gold rush, and North Carolina led the country in gold production until the California rush of 1849.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: America's first gold rush started in a Carolina creek, not California.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a farm boy in 1799 holding a large dull-gold rock beside a shallow Carolina creek, wooden farmstead behind him, sunlight glinting on the rock. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The 1799 Reed discovery began America's first gold rush - in North Carolina.
img.title: FIRST GOLD RUSH

questions.question: Raleigh became North Carolina's permanent capital in 1792. Why was the site chosen?
questions.correctAnswer: It sat near the geographic center of the state, chosen so the capital would be within reach of all regions
distractors: It was the state's largest port city
It was the hometown of Governor Richard Caswell
It was where the Declaration of Rights was written
questions.explanation: After years of a moving capital, the state bought land in Wake County in 1792 and laid out Raleigh as a planned capital city, named for Sir Walter Raleigh. Its inland, central location served the whole state better than the coastal towns, and the present State Capitol opened there in 1840.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Raleigh was planned on purpose - central, inland, and named for Sir Walter.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of surveyors in the 1790s laying out a grid of streets for a planned capital city in a pine forest clearing, chains and compasses in hand, a wooden tavern nearby. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Raleigh was a planned capital, placed near the center of the state in 1792.
img.title: A PLANNED CAPITAL

questions.question: The present North Carolina State Capitol in Raleigh, completed in 1840, is unusual among state capitols because:
questions.correctAnswer: It is a preserved 19th-century building that today houses only the governor's and lieutenant governor's offices - the legislature meets in its own building nearby
distractors: It is built entirely of wood in Greek Revival style
It still serves as the meeting place of the General Assembly
It was moved brick by brick from New Bern
questions.explanation: The 1840 Greek Revival capitol is a National Historic Landmark. Since 1963 the General Assembly has met in the separate Legislative Building, making North Carolina one of the few states whose historic capitol no longer houses the legislature.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The old Capitol keeps the governor; lawmakers meet across the street.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a dignified Greek Revival state capitol building with a low dome and stone columns in a green square, oak trees and a modern legislative building visible in the distance. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: The 1840 Capitol now holds the governor's office; the legislature has its own building.
img.title: THE 1840 CAPITOL

questions.question: During the early 1800s, North Carolina earned an unflattering nickname - the 'Rip Van Winkle State.' It meant the state was:
questions.correctAnswer: Asleep - falling behind its neighbors because it neglected schools, roads, and ports
distractors: Famous for producing sleepy tobacco
The last state to build any towns
Known for its long winter hibernation
questions.explanation: With poor roads, shallow ports, and few public schools, thousands of North Carolinians left for other states. Reformers like Archibald Murphey pushed internal improvements and public education in response, and by the 1850s railroads and schools had begun to wake the state up.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'Rip Van Winkle State' = asleep while neighbors moved ahead.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a muddy early 1800s Carolina wagon road with a stuck farm wagon, contrasted with a new railroad and steam locomotive being built on the horizon, a one-room schoolhouse nearby. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: NC was mocked as asleep for neglecting roads, ports, and schools.
img.title: RIP VAN WINKLE STATE

questions.question: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, chartered in 1789, is distinguished as the:
questions.correctAnswer: Oldest public university in the United States - the first to open its doors to students, in 1795
distractors: First university in the United States of any kind

questions.question: The 1835 North Carolina constitutional convention made an important democratic change: it provided for:
questions.correctAnswer: The governor to be elected directly by the people instead of by the legislature
distractors: All adult men to vote regardless of property for every office
Women to vote in state elections
The abolition of property requirements for the state Senate
questions.explanation: Under the 1776 constitution, the General Assembly chose the governor. The 1835 amendments let voters elect the governor directly - a major step toward popular government - though the same convention shamefully stripped free Black men of the vote they had previously held.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1835 - the people, not the legislature, would pick the governor.

questions.question: In the decades before the Civil War, most North Carolina farms produced:
questions.correctAnswer: Food crops, tobacco, and naval stores such as tar and turpentine from the longleaf pine forests
distractors: Cotton on huge plantations worked by thousands
Rice in flooded coastal paddies
Indigo for export to British dye works
questions.explanation: North Carolina's tar, pitch, and turpentine - naval stores from longleaf pines - were so important that 'Tar Heel' traditions trace to the products. Most farms were small and raised corn, wheat, livestock, and tobacco rather than running vast cotton plantations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tar, turpentine, and tobacco - the working crops of old NC farms.

questions.correctAnswer: Held their position in battle as if tar had stuck their heels to the ground - they refused to retreat
distractors: Marched barefoot because their shoes were coated in tar
Worked in tar pits between battles to supply the navy
Painted their heels black as a regimental badge
questions.explanation: In one famous version, after a battle in which NC troops held firm while others fell back, General Robert E. Lee praised them and the name stuck: North Carolinians clung to their ground 'like tar on their heels.' Tar production gives the nickname a second, older root.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tar Heels stuck fast - in the tar woods and on the battlefield.

questions.question: North Carolina was the LAST Confederate state to secede from the Union, in May 1861. The best explanation is:
questions.correctAnswer: Most North Carolinians were reluctant; the state left only after the firing on Fort Sumter and Lincoln's call for troops to invade the South
distractors: North Carolina's governor supported the Union and had to be removed first
The state's convention could not meet because of a smallpox outbreak
North Carolina waited for a promise that Raleigh would be the Confederate capital
questions.explanation: Unionist feeling ran strong in North Carolina, and voters had even rejected calling a secession convention in February 1861. After Fort Sumter and the federal call for troops to march against the seceded states, sentiment flipped, and NC seceded on May 20, 1861 - ironically, the celebrated Mecklenburg date.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Last out - NC seceded only after Sumter and the call for troops.

questions.question: During the Civil War, North Carolina contributed more soldiers to the Confederacy than any other southern state - and also suffered:
questions.correctAnswer: The most Confederate deaths of any state, about 40,000 men
distractors: The destruction of its capital by fire
A naval blockade that starved its entire coast
Defeat in every battle fought on its soil
questions.explanation: North Carolina furnished roughly 125,000 troops - more than its voting population - and lost about 40,000, the highest death toll of any Confederate state. The losses touched nearly every community in the state and shaped its memory of the war for generations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: First at Bethel, farthest at Gettysburg, last at Appomattox - and the heaviest losses.

questions.question: Fort Fisher, guarding the Cape Fear River below Wilmington, was vital to the Confederacy because it:
questions.correctAnswer: Protected blockade-running ships bringing supplies through Wilmington, the South's last major open port
distractors: Housed the Confederate treasury and archives
Was the largest shipyard in the Confederacy
Guarded the railroad bridge to Richmond's factories
questions.explanation: Called the 'Gibraltar of the Confederacy,' the massive earthen fort kept the Cape Fear open to fast blockade runners carrying food, weapons, and medicine. When Fort Fisher finally fell in January 1865, Wilmington closed and the Confederacy's supply line was cut.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fort Fisher kept Wilmington open - the South's last lifeline.

questions.question: The largest land battle fought in North Carolina during the Civil War was the Battle of Bentonville (March 1865), which ended with:
questions.correctAnswer: Confederate General Joseph Johnston's army retreating, weeks before he surrendered to Sherman in North Carolina
distractors: A Confederate victory that saved Raleigh from capture
The capture of General Sherman by Confederate cavalry
The burning of the state capitol by retreating troops
questions.explanation: At Bentonville, Johnston made a last attempt to stop Sherman's march through the Carolinas. Outnumbered, he withdrew after three days of fighting. Just over a month later he surrendered his army - the largest surrender of the war - at Bennett Place near Durham.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bentonville was NC's biggest battle - and nearly its last.

questions.correctAnswer: Confederate General Joseph Johnston surrendered nearly 90,000 soldiers to Union General William Sherman - the largest troop surrender of the war
distractors: Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia
The peace treaty between the United States and Britain was signed
North Carolina voted to return to the Union
questions.explanation: After Lee's surrender at Appomattox, Johnston met Sherman at James Bennett's farmhouse and, on April 26, 1865, surrendered all Confederate forces in the Carolinas, Georgia, and Florida - about 89,000 men, more than at Appomattox. North Carolina hosted the war's largest surrender.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The biggest surrender happened at a NC farmhouse - Bennett Place.

questions.question: North Carolina's 1868 constitution, written during Reconstruction, was revolutionary for the state because it:
questions.correctAnswer: Abolished property qualifications for voting, gave all adult men the vote, and required free public schools for all children
distractors: Moved the capital back to New Bern
Made the governor serve for life terms
Banned all private schools in the state
questions.explanation: The 1868 convention - which included Black delegates for the first time - produced a democratic constitution: universal male suffrage, popular election of judges and county officials, and a mandate for a free public school system. Much of its framework survives in North Carolina's government today.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1868 - vote without property, schools for all children.

questions.question: During Reconstruction, Black North Carolinians exercised political power for the first time - for example, they:
questions.correctAnswer: Won election to the General Assembly, Congress, and local offices across the state
distractors: Were appointed to the state Supreme Court for life
Formed a separate government in the mountains
Controlled the state Democratic Party convention
questions.explanation: Freedmen voted and held office throughout Reconstruction: 15 Black men served as delegates in the 1868 convention, and Black legislators, congressmen such as John Adams Hyman, and local officials helped govern. This era of Black political power was later cut down by violence and, by 1900, by disfranchisement laws.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Reconstruction opened the ballot - and Black Carolinians won real office.

questions.question: North Carolina's current constitution dates from 1971. It is the state's:
questions.correctAnswer: Third constitution, following those of 1776 and 1868 (as amended)
distractors: First constitution ever adopted
Fifth constitution, following four colonial charters
Second constitution, following only the 1868 document
questions.explanation: North Carolina has governed under three constitutions: 1776, 1868 (heavily amended in 1871 and after), and the current constitution approved by voters in 1970 and effective in 1971. All three keep the Declaration of Rights as Article I.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Three constitutions - 1776, 1868, 1971. The current one is number three.

questions.question: In North Carolina's government, the General Assembly is the branch that:
questions.correctAnswer: Makes the laws - it is the state legislature, made up of a Senate and a House of Representatives
distractors: Enforces the laws and commands the highway patrol
Interprets the laws in the state court system
Elects the governor every four years
questions.explanation: The General Assembly is North Carolina's lawmaking branch, like Congress at the national level. It meets in the Legislative Building in Raleigh and writes the statutes, passes the state budget, and can propose constitutional amendments.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: General Assembly = lawmaking. Think 'state Congress' in Raleigh.

170 - a Senate of 70 and a House of 100
203 - a Senate of 50 and a House of 153
questions.explanation: The NC Senate has 50 members and the NC House of Representatives has 120, for a total of 170 legislators. questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 50 plus 120 makes 170 in the General Assembly.

Six years for senators and two for representatives
Four years for senators and two for representatives
questions.explanation: Unlike the United States Congress, where senators serve six years, every member of North Carolina's General Assembly - senators and representatives alike - serves a two-year term and faces the voters in every even-year election.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In Raleigh everyone runs every two years.

questions.question: North Carolina's governor is the head of which branch, and what is the governor's main job?
questions.correctAnswer: The executive branch - carrying out the laws, proposing the state budget, and commanding the National Guard unless it is federalized
distractors: The judicial branch - hearing the state's final appeals
The legislative branch - presiding over the state Senate daily
The executive branch - writing all state laws personally
questions.explanation: The governor leads the executive branch: enforcing laws, directing state agencies, preparing the recommended budget, and serving as commander-in-chief of the NC National Guard. The governor cannot write laws - that power belongs to the General Assembly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Governor = executive. Laws are made by the Assembly, carried out by the governor.

questions.question: North Carolina's governor was the last in the nation to receive veto power. When did that happen?
questions.correctAnswer: Voters approved it in 1996, and the first veto was cast in 2002

Voters approved it in 1868 during Reconstruction
It has never been granted - NC governors still have no veto
questions.explanation: For 220 years North Carolina's governor had no veto at all - the weakest governorship in America on paper. questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: NC was last - the veto arrived only in 1996.

questions.correctAnswer: Council of State, including the lieutenant governor, attorney general, secretary of state, and treasurer
distractors: State Board of Elections, which runs all county offices
Supreme Court of North Carolina
Governor's Cabinet, appointed by the governor
questions.explanation: The Council of State is NC's plural executive: the governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, attorney general, state treasurer, state auditor, superintendent of public instruction, and the commissioners of agriculture, insurance, and labor - each elected statewide and independent of the governor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ten elected executives - the Council of State shares executive power.

questions.question: In North Carolina courts, the Supreme Court of North Carolina is:
questions.correctAnswer: The state's highest court, with a chief justice and six associate justices elected by the voters

A trial court that hears cases with juries in each county
Part of the federal court system for the Southeast
questions.explanation: North Carolina's Supreme Court has seven justices - a chief justice and six associates - elected statewide to eight-year terms. It is the final word on North Carolina law, and beneath it sits the Court of Appeals, whose 15 judges hear cases in panels of three.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Seven elected justices sit on NC's highest court.

67 counties

questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One hundred counties - a perfectly round number for NC.

questions.correctAnswer: The sheriff, elected by the county's voters to lead law enforcement

The police chief of the county seat
The superintendent of the county schools
questions.explanation: North Carolina voters elect their sheriff, register of deeds, and clerk of superior court, while the county manager is a professional hired by the elected board of commissioners. Understanding which officials answer directly to voters is a core part of NC local government.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sheriffs answer to voters; county managers answer to commissioners.

questions.correctAnswer: Made the first successful powered airplane flights in history - which is why NC license plates say 'First in Flight'
distractors: Flew the first airplane across the Atlantic Ocean
Broke the sound barrier for the first time
Launched the first American rocket into space
questions.explanation: The Wright brothers chose Kitty Hawk for its steady winds, soft sand, and privacy. Orville's first flight lasted 12 seconds; the fourth flight that day covered 852 feet. North Carolina claims the honor as the state where powered flight began.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: First in Flight - Kitty Hawk, December 17, 1903, twelve seconds that changed the world.

The governor offered them a cash prize to fly there
It was the closest beach to their Ohio bicycle shop

Automobiles and airplane engines
Coal mining and oil refining

The world's tallest chair factory chimney stood there
Furniture was invented in High Point in 1889

Civil War soldiers carried the seeds from Cuba

Spanish submarines based in Cuba

Led immediately to a federal law ending all segregation
Were the first protest ever held in North Carolina

A method invented by the governor of North Carolina

She can never withdraw the money again

questions.explanation: Bank deposits earn interest - the bank pays her for the use of her money - and deposits are insured by the FDIC up to $250,000. Cash at home earns nothing and can be lost, stolen, or spent on impulse.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In a bank, savings grow with interest and sleep safely insured.

questions.question: Two stores sell the same game console. Store A charges $300 cash. Store B offers it for $25 a month for 18 months on credit, totaling $450. The extra $150 at Store B is best described as:
questions.correctAnswer: The cost of credit - interest and fees paid for the privilege of buying now and paying over time
distractors: A sales tax charged by the state
A warranty the store adds automatically
A discount for loyal customers
questions.explanation: Credit is never free: paying over time adds interest and fees, here $150 - half again the cash price. Comparing the total cost of credit against the cash price is one of the most valuable habits in personal finance (8.E.1.4).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Credit charges rent on money - always compare the total, not the monthly payment.

Tags kept blank without writing. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Buying on credit costs extra - compare the total price, not the payment.
img.title: THE TRUE COST OF CREDIT

questions.question: A checking account and a savings account are both useful, but they serve different purposes. The best summary is:
questions.correctAnswer: Checking is for everyday spending and paying bills; savings is for goals and emergencies and usually earns more interest
distractors: Checking accounts are only for adults over 25
Savings accounts cannot hold more than $100
Both accounts pay exactly the same interest and have no differences
questions.explanation: Checking accounts are built for frequent transactions - debit cards, bill pay, transfers. Savings accounts are built to hold money apart for goals and emergencies, typically paying higher interest but limiting easy access. Smart households use both.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Checking spends, savings waits - two accounts, two jobs.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of two clearly different piggy-bank style containers on a shelf, one plain for daily use with a debit card beside it and one larger with a small padlock, morning kitchen light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: Checking is for spending; savings is for goals and earns more interest.
img.title: TWO ACCOUNTS, TWO JOBS

questions.question: Jordan has $60. He can buy a ticket to a concert tonight or save the money toward a $240 bike he needs for his paper route job. In economics, the $60 concert ticket's true cost includes its opportunity cost, which is:
questions.correctAnswer: The value of the next-best use he gives up - progress toward the bike and the job earnings it would bring
distractors: Only the $60 printed on the ticket
The price of popcorn at the concert
The wages the performers earn that night
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the most valuable alternative you give up. Choosing the concert costs not just $60 but also delayed earnings from the paper route the bike would make possible - the kind of trade-off analysis standard 8.E.1.4 asks students to make.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Every choice costs the best alternative - that is opportunity cost.

img.tip: Opportunity cost = the best alternative you give up.
img.title: WHAT YOU GIVE UP

questions.question: Why do financial advisors recommend keeping an emergency fund before investing in the stock market?
questions.correctAnswer: Emergencies are certain to happen eventually, and money needed soon must be safe and available - investments can lose value at the wrong moment
distractors: The stock market is illegal for people with savings accounts
Emergency funds pay higher returns than any investment
Banks require an emergency fund before opening any account
questions.explanation: Car repairs, medical bills, and job losses arrive without warning. An emergency fund of a few months' expenses, kept in insured savings, prevents a crisis from becoming debt. Only money not needed for years belongs in investments whose value rises and falls.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Safety first, investing second - emergencies do not check the stock market.

img.scene: Mature educational illustration of a sturdy umbrella sheltering a family budget desk from a sudden rainstorm outside the window, a labeled-looking jar kept blank on the desk, calm inside. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: An emergency fund keeps a crisis from becoming debt.
img.title: THE EMERGENCY UMBRELLA

questions.question: Economists say education and training increase a worker's 'human capital.' In North Carolina's modern economy this means:
questions.correctAnswer: Workers with more skills and credentials usually qualify for higher-paying jobs in fields like technology, health care, and finance
distractors: Employers must pay everyone the same salary
College graduates never face unemployment for any reason
Only factory jobs require any training at all
questions.explanation: As NC's economy shifted from textiles and tobacco toward research, banking, and medicine, the premium on skills rose. Education - degrees, certifications, apprenticeships - raises a worker's productivity and earning power over a lifetime, which is why it is called investing in human capital.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Skills are capital you carry in your head - and they pay interest for life.

img.tip: Education builds human capital - skills that raise lifetime earnings.
img.title: SKILLS THAT PAY

questions.question: A drought cuts North Carolina's sweet potato harvest in half while demand stays the same. Using supply and demand, prices will most likely:
questions.correctAnswer: Rise, because the smaller supply of sweet potatoes is scarcer relative to demand
distractors: Fall, because farmers will sell at any price
Stay exactly the same by state law
Rise only if the governor orders it
questions.explanation: When supply falls and demand is unchanged, buyers compete for fewer goods and bid prices up. The same model explains the opposite: a bumper crop with flat demand pushes prices down - the cycle NC farmers watch every season.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Less supply, same demand - prices climb. It is the market's seesaw.

img.tip: When supply shrinks and demand holds, prices rise.
img.title: SUPPLY, DEMAND, PRICE

questions.question: Urbanization has reshaped North Carolina over the past century. Which statement best describes the change?
questions.correctAnswer: Most North Carolinians once lived in rural areas and small towns; today most live in and around cities and suburbs
distractors: Cities have shrunk steadily since 1900 while farms doubled
Urbanization means everyone now works in agriculture
North Carolina has no cities larger than 50,000 people
questions.explanation: In 1900 North Carolina was overwhelmingly rural. Factory jobs, then office, research, and service jobs, drew people to Charlotte, the Triangle, the Triad, and other metros. Today a majority of North Carolinians live in urban areas - changing the state's politics, traffic, housing, and land use (standard 8.G).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: From farm fields to city skylines - NC urbanized within a few generations.

img.tip: NC flipped from mostly rural to mostly urban in a century.

questions.question: Charlotte Douglas International and Raleigh-Durham International (RDU) are important to North Carolina mainly because they:
questions.correctAnswer: Link the state's business and research centers to the nation and world, supporting jobs and trade
distractors: Are the two largest military air bases in the country
Were the sites of the Wright brothers' first flights
Handle only mail and cargo, never passengers
questions.explanation: Major airports are economic engines: Charlotte Douglas is one of the busiest airports in the world as an American Airlines hub, and RDU serves the Research Triangle's universities and companies. Together with interstates and ports, they knit NC into national and global networks (8.G).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Big airports keep NC connected - and connection means jobs.

questions.question: Singer and pianist Nina Simone, born Eunice Waymon in Tryon, North Carolina, used her fame during the 1960s to:
questions.correctAnswer: Write and perform songs that became anthems of the civil rights movement, such as 'Mississippi Goddam'
distractors: Serve as North Carolina's secretary of state
Found the Research Triangle Park music institute
Refuse to perform anywhere in the South for her whole career
questions.explanation: Born in the mountain town of Tryon and trained as a classical pianist with help from her community, Nina Simone fused jazz, blues, and classical music. After the Birmingham church bombing and Medgar Evers's murder, her protest songs made her a defining voice of the movement.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: From Tryon to the movement - Nina Simone turned music into protest.

questions.question: Why has North Carolina replaced its constitution twice (1776, then 1868, then re-adopted a modernized one in 1971) while keeping a Declaration of Rights in every version?
questions.correctAnswer: Each generation rewrote the frame of government to fit its times - war, emancipation, modernization - but held fast to the principle that rights come before government power
distractors: The United States required every state to rewrite its constitution each century
Each new governor demanded a personal constitution
The Declaration of Rights was copied by accident into later documents
questions.explanation: Constitutions balance change and continuity. North Carolina rewrote its frame after independence, after the Civil War and emancipation, and again to modernize in 1971 - but all three documents open by declaring the people's rights, a continuity stretching from Halifax in 1776 to today (8.C&G.1.1).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Governments get rebuilt; rights stay first - that is the NC tradition.

questions.question: A historian argues that North Carolina's story is 'firsts that changed the nation.' Which set of evidence best supports that claim using only events from this course?
questions.correctAnswer: First official call for independence (Halifax Resolves), first powered flight (Kitty Hawk), and the sit-in that launched a national movement (Greensboro)
distractors: First gold rush in California, first transatlantic flight, and the first moon landing
First state to ratify the US Constitution, first to secede, and first to elect a president
First English colony at Jamestown, first battle of the Civil War, and the first national park
questions.explanation: Each item is a documented North Carolina first with national consequences: the Halifax Resolves pushed the colonies toward declaring independence, the Wright brothers opened the air age, and four students in Greensboro ignited the sit-in movement that helped dismantle segregation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Halifax, Kitty Hawk, Greensboro - three NC firsts that moved a nation.
